preamble: Nasalization of the open vowel /a/ to [ã] arises when the velum lowers in anticipation of an adjacent nasal consonant; when the conditioning nasal is later lost, the nasality is left on the vowel as a contrastive feature. Portuguese lã 'wool' (< Latin lāna) and Hindi dā̃t 'tooth' (< Sanskrit danta) both show a low vowel that absorbed a following nasal consonant.
phoneticEffects: Nasalization, Regressive Assimilation, Nasal Consonant Loss, Phonemicization

examples.note: Intervocalic /n/ nasalized the preceding /a/ and was lost (Old Galician-Portuguese lãa > lã); the modern vowel is a raised nasal [ɐ̃].
The nasal of the cluster -nt- was absorbed into the preceding vowel, which became long and nasalized.
